subject: social batteries

hook.say: There are four kinds of social battery. One of them never needs charging.

types.name: The Introvert
types.say: Charges alone. Spends in public.

types.name: The Extrovert
types.say: Charges in public. Spends alone.

types.name: The Ambivert
types.say: Charges anywhere, depending on the week you've had.

types.name: The Omnivert
types.say: Fully charged, then completely done, with no warning at all.

kicker.say: Most people are the middle two. You're not broken. You're just social in a different order.

caption: Which battery are you? For most people it isn't one. It's a rotation. Save this and send it to the friend who never replies.

subject: being wrong

hook.say: When you're wrong, there are four reactions. Only one of them keeps your friends.

types.name: The Defender
types.say: You argue the point until everyone gives up. Then you think about it all night.
types.tag: wins the room, loses the night

types.name: The Learner
types.say: You say oh, good point, and actually mean it. That's rarer than it sounds.

types.name: The Blamer
types.say: It was the instructions. It was the timing. It was never you.

types.name: The Avoider
types.say: You go quiet, agree in the moment, and quietly keep doing it your way.

kicker.say: Being wrong is free information. Most people pay for it with a fight.

caption: Which one are you when you're wrong? Most people are a defender at work and a learner with strangers.

subject: taking a compliment

hook.say: Someone compliments you. There are four ways people ruin it.

types.name: The Deflector
types.say: You immediately explain why it wasn't actually that good.

types.name: The Absorber
types.say: You say thank you. That's it. Somehow that's the uncomfortable one.

types.name: The Suspect
types.say: You assume they want something. Nobody's ever just nice.

types.name: The Joker
types.say: You make a joke before anyone can take it seriously.

kicker.say: A compliment is a gift. You're allowed to keep it.

caption: Which one do you do? Deflecting a compliment is just telling someone their taste is wrong.

subject: unanswered texts

hook.say: There are four types of person, and they all handle an awkward text differently.

types.name: The Instant Replier
types.say: You answer in nine seconds so nobody can be annoyed with you.

types.name: The Overthinker
types.say: You draft it eleven times and send it three days later.

types.name: The Ghoster
types.say: You decide the conversation ended itself.

types.name: The Drafter
types.say: You write the perfect reply. You never send it. It lives in your head forever.

kicker.say: An unanswered message is usually not rejection. It's just a phone face down.

caption: Be honest, which one are you? The overthinker and the drafter are the same person with different confidence levels.

subject: being alone

hook.say: Being alone feels different for four kinds of people. And only one of them is actually lonely.

types.name: The Recharger
types.say: Alone is where you become useful again.

types.name: The Filler
types.say: You put something on, anything, so the room isn't quiet.

types.name: The Avoider
types.say: You keep busy so you never have to find out how you actually feel.

types.name: The Missing
types.say: You're alone and fine, until you remember who used to be there.

kicker.say: Loneliness isn't the absence of people. It's the absence of being known.

caption: You can be alone and not lonely, or surrounded and completely lonely. Which one is yours lately?

subject: what silence means

hook.say: Silence means four completely different things. Read the room.

types.name: The Processing
types.say: Give them a minute. They're building the sentence.

types.name: The Hurt
types.say: They're not quiet. They're waiting to see if you notice.

types.name: The Done
types.say: They've decided this conversation isn't worth the energy anymore.

types.name: The Overloaded
types.say: Too many people, too much noise. Nothing personal.

kicker.say: Most arguments are two people reading the same silence differently.

caption: The worst part of silence is that you always fill it with your own fear first. Usually that's all it is.
